title: Foundations
blurb: What sits in a Webex organization, which protocols the calling path actually uses, and which documents this lab will trust.

lessons.title: The Webex platform map
lessons.summary: Control Hub is the admin surface. Calling, meetings, messaging, devices, Contact Center, and Dedicated Instance are services of one organization, not separate products with separate identity stores.
objectives: Name the admin portal
Separate multi-tenant calling from Dedicated Instance
Place Contact Center and devices on the same map

diagram.caption: Control Hub administers Calling, Dedicated Instance, Contact Center, and devices.

steps.label: Sign in
steps.detail: The customer view is the organization you are about to change.
steps.inspect: GET https://admin.webex.com as a full administrator.

steps.label: Open Calling
steps.detail: Locations, PSTN, features, and Dedicated Instance live under Calling.

steps.label: Open Contact Center
steps.detail: Flows and queues are a different service from Webex Calling call queues.
steps.inspect: Contact Center service, not Calling > Features > Call Queue

steps.label: Open Devices
steps.detail: Phones and RoomOS devices are claimed into the same organization.

paragraphs: Administrators work in Control Hub. Webex Calling configuration, including locations and PSTN, is documented as an organization-level task, not a per-phone task.

Dedicated Instance is an add-on to Webex Calling. It includes Unified CM, optional IM and Presence, Unity Connection, Expressway, and Emergency Responder in the Americas. It is not a second Control Hub.
A Webex Calling call queue is a calling feature for a location. A Webex Contact Center queue is a routing object used by Flow Designer and the agent desktop.
Mixing those names in a design review is how a hunt-pilot migration lands in the wrong product. The migration tools for Unified CM features produce Calling CSVs, not Contact Center flows.

lessons.title: Three calling models
lessons.summary: Multi-tenant Webex Calling, Dedicated Instance, and on-premises Unified CM can all exist in one design. The local gateway is how the premises system meets the cloud.
objectives: Contrast the three call-control homes
Say what the local gateway is for
Remember the interop trunk into Dedicated Instance

steps.detail: Unmatched calls go to the local gateway for that premises path.

paragraphs: Multi-tenant Webex Calling hosts the users you configure with locations, numbers, and calling features in Control Hub.

Dedicated Instance is still Unified CM, Unity Connection, and Expressway, deployed by Cisco in a private instance and cross-launched from Control Hub. On-premises Unified CM stays yours, including the dial plan and the PSTN gateways you already run.
The configuration workflow describes the local gateway as the enterprise or partner edge for PSTN and for legacy PBX interworking, including Unified CM.
Cisco's hypothetical Dedicated Instance stories are labeled hypothetical. Use them as architecture patterns, not as claims about a named customer.

lessons.title: SIP and E.164 for this cloud
lessons.summary: Webex Calling speaks SIP. Numbers that cross a trunk are safest in +E.164. This lesson is the minimum signaling vocabulary the rest of the lab assumes.
objectives: Read a SIP INVITE as a request, not a string dump
Write a number in +E.164
Know which RFC names the tel URI

diagram.caption: An INVITE carries a request-URI. +E.164 is the form Unified CM and Webex Calling exchange.

flow.title: From a dialing habit to a SIP request

steps.label: Digits
steps.detail: The user dials an extension, a national number, or an emergency number. The location's dialing settings decide what those digits mean.
steps.inspect: External dial digit, extension length, routing prefix

steps.label: Match or miss
steps.detail: Enterprise dial plans match patterns and choose a trunk or route group.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.detail: SIP is the session protocol. RFC 3261 defines the request that starts a dialog.

steps.label: +E.164
steps.detail: The workflow guide expects Unified CM to normalize to +E.164 so one set of route patterns covers every dialing habit.

sections.h: SIP is the session, not the audio
paragraphs: RFC 3261 defines SIP methods such as INVITE, ACK, BYE, and REGISTER, and the response classes 1xx through 6xx. Media is separate, most often RTP protected with SRTP.
A local gateway failure is often a SIP failure: TLS handshake, certificate name, or a trunk that never registers. The audio codecs do not matter until the dialog exists.

ITU-T E.164 is the international public numbering plan. Writing a number as + followed by the country code and the national number is the form Cisco's Webex Calling workflow uses between Unified CM and the cloud.
RFC 3966 defines the tel URI. You will see both tel and sip forms in traces. Do not invent a private numbering plan and call it E.164.

quiz.q: Which RFC defines SIP?
quiz.why: RFC 3261 is the SIP specification. The others are location, HELD, and ICE.

quiz.q: +E.164 refers to
choices: The ITU-T international public numbering plan, written with a leading +
quiz.why: E.164 is the ITU recommendation. The Webex workflow uses the + form.

quiz.q: The tel URI is specified in
quiz.why: RFC 3966 is the tel URI.

quiz.q: SRTP is
quiz.why: The port reference lists SRTP media toward Webex Calling. RFC 3711 specifies SRTP.

quiz.q: In the Unified CM integration guide, dialing habits are handled by
choices: Normalizing to +E.164 and using one set of route patterns
A different route pattern for every possible habit with no normalization
quiz.why: The workflow article describes normalization translation patterns and +E.164 route patterns.

quiz.q: A 200 response in SIP means
quiz.why: SIP response classes are part of RFC 3261. 2xx is success.

cards.back: The SIP request that asks to open a session.
Country code plus national number, with a leading plus.
The tel URI.
The profile that encrypts RTP. RFC 3711.

fault.title: A trace full of 403
fault.symptom: The local gateway answers the INVITE with 403 and the call never rings.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: SIP/2.0 403 Forbidden, Reason: certificate name mismatch on the trunk FQDN.
fault.cause: The name Webex Calling expects on the certificate is not the name presented. The trunk article shows CN or SAN must match the FQDN or SRV identity.
fault.fix: Present a certificate whose CN or SAN matches the trunk address, then retest one call.

lessons.title: Identity, directory sync, and SSO
lessons.summary: Control Hub is the identity service for Webex. Dedicated Instance users sync from that directory, and Cisco says that path requires single sign-on.
objectives: Say where the Webex identity lives
Explain the SSO requirement for Dedicated Instance directory sync
Separate a user from a workspace

diagram.caption: Directory sync lands in Control Hub. Dedicated Instance Unified CM syncs from there when SSO is on.

flow.title: A new hire becomes a calling user

steps.label: Sync the user
steps.detail: Control Hub directory synchronization is shared by meetings, calling, and Dedicated Instance.

steps.label: Assign Calling
steps.detail: A calling license is what lets you give the user a number and calling features. Professional, Standard, and Workspace are not the same.

steps.label: Sync onward
steps.detail: Dedicated Instance Unified CM synchronizes from Control Hub. Cisco says this user sync works only when SSO is enabled.
steps.inspect: Without SSO, directory sync is not supported

steps.label: Activation
steps.detail: Contact Center user actions include sending an activation email. That is a different license from Webex Calling.

sections.h: SSO is not optional for that sync
paragraphs: The Dedicated Instance deployment-models article says end-user data is synchronized with Control Hub, and Dedicated Instance Unified CM then synchronizes from Control Hub.

The same article says the user synchronization feature functions only when single sign-on is enabled. Without SSO, directory synchronization is not supported. Native Unified CM user options still exist.

The license article assigns Webex Calling licenses to users or to workspaces. A workspace is for a shared device, not for a person's soft client, and the matrix shows soft clients as unavailable on workspace licenses.
Do not create a human as a workspace to save a license. The feature set, including shared lines and virtual lines, differs.

quiz.why: The deployment-models article states the SSO requirement.

choices: Shared across meetings, calling, and Dedicated Instance
quiz.why: The article calls it a shared feature across those Webex services.

quiz.q: A workspace license is for
choices: Shared devices such as common-area phones, not a person's full soft-client calling
quiz.why: The license article describes the workspace license as shared-use and not for an individual user's calling needs.

quiz.q: A Contact Center activation email is
choices: A user-management action for Contact Center administrators
The same click as a calling license
quiz.why: The roles article lists sending an activation email among Contact Center user actions.

quiz.q: Native Unified CM user import on Dedicated Instance
choices: Still exists, alongside the Control Hub path
quiz.why: The article says Dedicated Instance also supports native on-premises Unified CM user sync options.

cards.back: Cisco says Control Hub user sync into Dedicated Instance requires SSO.
A place license for shared devices, not a substitute for a person.
The directory Webex services share.
How a Contact Center user is invited, separate from a calling license.

lessons.title: Ports, media, and certificates
lessons.summary: Certificate trunks and registration trunks do not use the same signaling port. Media has its own UDP ranges, and ICE can take the cloud relay out of the path.
objectives: Quote the two signaling ports
Separate optimized media ports for the app and for devices
Know that a third-party SBC local gateway is certificate-based

diagram.caption: TCP 5062 and TCP 8934 are different trunk types. Media is UDP.

steps.label: SIP TLS
steps.detail: Outbound signaling uses TCP 5062 for a certificate-based trunk and TCP 8934 for a registration-based trunk.

steps.label: Trunk identity
steps.detail: The trunk article assumes the gateway listens on TLS 5061 unless you choose another listen port, and the certificate CN or SAN must match the FQDN or SRV.

steps.label: Optimized media
steps.detail: If ICE succeeds inside the organization, media can go direct. The app uses UDP 8500-8699, audio 8500-8599 and video 8600-8699.

steps.label: Device media
steps.detail: Devices that optimize media use UDP 19560-19661 in the port reference's example.
steps.inspect: Site firewalls must allow the range both ways

paragraphs: The port reference says TCP 5062 is required for a certificate-based trunk and TCP 8934 for a registration-based trunk. Opening only 5061 on the firewall does not satisfy either cloud destination.
The trunk guide's listen port of 5061 is the port on your gateway, not the cloud destination port. Read the column headings before you copy a number into a firewall ticket.

cite.label: Trunks, route groups, and dial plans

paragraphs: Cisco states that a third-party SBC acting as a local gateway is supported only with a certificate-based trunk, and only for SBCs that appear in the Control Hub device-type list.

ICE is RFC 8445. When it succeeds, the port reference says the cloud media relay is removed and the endpoints talk directly. That is why an inside firewall can still break a call that signaled correctly.

quiz.q: Certificate-based trunk signaling to Webex Calling uses
quiz.why: The port reference assigns 5062 to certificate-based trunks.

quiz.q: Registration-based trunk signaling uses
quiz.why: The port reference assigns 8934 to registration-based trunks.

quiz.q: The gateway listen port the trunk article assumes, unless you change it, is
quiz.why: The article says it assumes the standard TLS SIP port 5061 for the local gateway to receive signaling.

quiz.q: When ICE succeeds, Webex App direct media uses
quiz.why: The port reference gives that range, with audio and video splits inside it.

quiz.q: A third-party SBC local gateway is supported
choices: Only as a certificate-based trunk, and only if the SBC is in the Control Hub list
quiz.why: The trunk article states that limit.

quiz.q: ICE is specified by
quiz.why: RFC 8445 is Interactive Connectivity Establishment.

cards.back: Certificate-based trunk signaling to Webex Calling.
Registration-based trunk signaling to Webex Calling.
Optimized Webex App media in the port reference.
Certificate trunk only, and only a validated device type.

fault.title: Registered in the lab, dead in production
fault.symptom: A registration trunk works on a bench and fails after the firewall tightens to 5062 only.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: gateway, registration timeout, destination tcp/8934 denied.
fault.cause: Registration trunks need 8934. 5062 is the other trunk type.
fault.fix: Allow TCP 8934 to the Webex Calling signaling destinations in the port reference, or move the design to a certificate trunk and open 5062 instead. Do not open both and hope.

lessons.title: Professional, Standard, and Workspace
lessons.summary: Webex Calling has three license options. Device counts, soft clients, shared lines, virtual lines, and call queue membership are not uniform across them.
lessons.uncertainty: The call queue article and the license matrix do not describe the Workspace license with the same sentence. This lab reports both and does not pick a silent winner.
objectives: Name the three license options
Read a row of the feature matrix
Notice the tension between the queue article and the workspace row

diagram.caption: The license matrix, not the product brochure, decides whether a user can join a call queue.

flow.title: Assign a license, then test one feature

steps.label: Assign Professional
steps.detail: The matrix shows five devices and soft clients for a professional user.

steps.label: Assign Workspace
steps.detail: The workspace license is one device and is not for an individual user's calling.

steps.label: Add agents
steps.detail: The matrix marks call queue Yes for professional user and professional workspace, No for Standard, and Yes for the Workspace license.
steps.inspect: Check the row, not the product name alone

steps.label: Reconcile the articles
steps.detail: The call queue article also says the queue is part of the professional license. Read both pages before you promise a standard user a queue seat.

paragraphs: Cisco's matrix lists device entitlement as 5 for Professional user and Professional workspace, 1 for Standard, and 1 for Workspace. Shared lines are marked Yes (35) for both Professional columns and No for Standard and Workspace.

Virtual lines are marked Yes for Professional and No for Standard and Workspace. Soft clients are Yes for a Professional user, No for a Professional workspace, Yes for Standard if that user is on soft clients, and No for Workspace.
The same matrix marks Call Queue as Yes for Professional user, Professional workspace, and the Workspace license, and No for Standard.

The configure-call-queue article says call queue is part of the Webex Calling professional license. Those two pages do not use identical wording. Treat the matrix as the feature grid and the queue article as the configuration guide, and recheck both before a design is frozen.

lessons.title: How to use this lab

steps.label: Open the link

paragraphs: Cisco's exam page for Implementing Cisco Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience (300-830 CLCCE) describes a 90-minute exam. Passing it earns Cisco Certified Specialist - Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience and can satisfy a CCNP Collaboration concentration.

Cisco Learning Network said the first date to test was 3 February 2026. The Essentials of Webex Calling (CLWXCALL) is a course, not that exam. Confirm dates on the live pages before you book anything.

sections.h: What this lab refuses to invent
paragraphs: Simulators do not claim Control Hub import compatibility. Boss logs are labeled synthetic. Hypothetical Dedicated Instance stories stay hypothetical.
When two Cisco pages use different wording, the lesson says so. That is a feature of the lab, not a broken link.
